title: La indirecta
goal: Realise you are being told off without being told off
culture: The indirecta is a whole grammar of complaint and the point of it is that nobody has to be embarrassed. Recognising it is the skill. Answering it directly — naming yourself, apologising outright — is a bigger breach than whatever you did.

beats.es: No es por nada, vecino, pero...
beats.objective: You know what is coming — let it come
beats.good: No es por nada means it is very much about something. When a sentence opens like this, what follows is about you.

beats.es: ...algunos sacan la basura el día que no toca, fíjese.
beats.good: Algunos — some people. There is exactly one person in the algunos and both of you know which one.

beats.es: Yo no digo nombres, ¿va? Yo no soy así.
beats.good: Naming yourself would embarrass her, and the entire architecture of the indirecta exists so that nobody has to be embarrassed. Play it straight.

beats.objective: Answer with what you will do
beats.say: Ya entendí, doña. Mañana la saco.
beats.en: I understand, doña. I’ll put it out tomorrow.
ok: ya entendi dona manana la saco
beats.good: Answer with the action and never with an admission. Say what you will do differently and the whole thing closes with neither of you having said it out loud.
